sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Paths and hand-picked logo sources
sections.what: Sets the input and output folders, loads the account list and any earlier manifest, and lists specific logo addresses for companies whose automatic icons were poor.
sections.why: The comments say automatic icons were too small or not identifiable for some companies, so specific sources were chosen.
sections.watch_out: The hand-picked addresses are third-party or archive links that can change or disappear.

sections.name: fetch
sections.title: Download one logo
sections.what: For one company, tries each logo source in turn, saves the first image that opens, and returns a record with its source and fingerprint. Accounts with no domain, or already saved from the same source, are skipped.
sections.why: Likely reason: several sources are tried because any one of them may fail or be missing.
sections.watch_out: Any error silently moves on to the next source, so a poor source can be used with no warning in the output.

summary: Downloads public company logos for the opportunity map, saves each as a PNG file, and writes a manifest recording where each logo came from.
purpose: Provide company logos for the opportunity map screens.
why: The docstring says it saves public site icons and must not expose private account information. Some companies have hand-picked logo sources because automatic icons were too small or unclear.
how: Reads the accounts list and the previous manifest. For each account with a domain, it tries the hand-picked source first, then several icon services, then the site's own favicon. The first one that opens as an image is saved as a PNG. Writes the manifest with the result for each account.
inputs: The accounts.json file, the previous manifest if one exists, and internet access to icon services and company sites.
outputs: PNG files in the capital-projects public opportunity-logos folder, and a manifest.json file listing each result.
risks: Logos come from third parties and archive links that may change or disappear. Only the first 500 KB of each download is read, so a larger image may fail to open. The license for using these logos is not stated in the code.
debug: Check the manifest status for each id. 'unavailable' means every source failed. If a logo is wrong, check the hand-picked source list. If nothing downloads, check the network and whether Pillow is installed.
